Detail columns and use cases

Source: vignettes/variables.Rmd
variables.Rmd

From data release 2026.2 on, pks_get() returns more than case counts and rates: the official name of every district, the district type, cases in which a firearm was used, and suspects by sex and nationality. This vignette describes these columns, the rules for using them, and a few typical analyses. All runnable examples use pks_example(), a small panel that ships with the package (five districts, two offence keys, 2019 to 2025), so they work without internet.

d <- pksR::pks_example()

The columns

Column Content Years
region_name_official District name of the BBSR crosswalk at the boundary year of the row; one name per district in a harmonized panel all
district_type District type as published: KfS (kreisfreie Stadt), LK (Landkreis), K (Kreis), SK (Stadtkreis), RV (Regionalverband) 2013 onwards
firearm_threatened Cases in which the suspect threatened with a firearm 2013 onwards
firearm_fired Cases in which a firearm was fired 2013 onwards
suspects_male, suspects_female Suspects by sex; together they give suspects 2013 onwards
suspects_non_german Non-German suspects (nichtdeutsche Tatverdächtige) 2013 onwards

The yearbooks of 2003 to 2012 publish none of the detail fields, so they are NA there. With data releases before 2026.2 all detail columns are NA, and pks_get() says so once per session. The percentages printed in the BKA tables (share of attempts, share of non-German suspects) are not included: they follow from the counts, and a percentage cannot be moved to another boundary with crosswalk weights, while counts can.

region_name stays the name as published, which changes in spelling between years (“SK Mülheim a.d.Ruhr”, “KfS Mülheim an der Ruhr”). region_name_official is the same for a district in every year of a harmonized panel and is the better choice for labels in tables and maps:

unique(d[, c("ags", "region_name", "region_name_official", "district_type")])
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   ags   region_name   region_name_official          district_type
#>   <chr> <chr>         <chr>                         <chr>        
#> 1 01001 Flensburg     Flensburg, Stadt              KfS          
#> 2 02000 Hamburg       Hamburg, Freie und Hansestadt KfS          
#> 3 03159 Göttingen     Göttingen                     LK           
#> 4 11000 Berlin        Berlin, Stadt                 KfS          
#> 5 16063 Wartburgkreis Wartburgkreis                 LK

Rules for the detail columns

  1. Suspects are persons, not cases. A person suspected of theft and of fraud counts under both keys, so suspect counts must never be summed over offence keys. Within one key they add up: suspects_male + suspects_female equals suspects. For keys that are computed as the difference of two published keys (890000 in 2014) the suspect columns are NA.
  2. Suspects are not offenders. A Tatverdächtiger is a person the police consider sufficiently suspected when the investigation ends. The PKS says nothing about charges or convictions.
  3. Non-German suspects are not only residents. They include people without residence in Germany (tourists, commuters, travelling offenders) and offences that only non-Germans can commit, such as offences against the Residence and the Asylum Acts (key 725000). Key 890000 (total offences excluding these) removes the second part. The PKS publishes no population by nationality; such denominators have to come from elsewhere, for example from INKAR through the package inkaR.
  4. Harmonized values can be fractional. Where a district was split, counts are divided with population or area weights and the row has estimated = TRUE. Districts changed by harmonization get their type in the latest table.
  5. Rates are recomputed, never averaged. pks_rates() recomputes the HZ for cases. Rates of the detail counts are computed the same way: sum the counts first, then divide by the population of the same rows.

Use case 1: cities and rural districts

Compare crime in cities (KfS) and rural districts (LK). The rate of a group is the sum of its cases over the sum of its population, not the mean of the district rates:

tot <- d[d$offence_key == "------", ]
tot$pop <- dplyr::coalesce(tot$population, tot$derived_population)
by_type <- dplyr::summarise(
  dplyr::group_by(tot, year, district_type),
  cases = sum(cases), pop = sum(pop), .groups = "drop"
)
by_type$hz <- by_type$cases / by_type$pop * 1e5
by_type[by_type$year == 2025, ]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>    year district_type  cases     pop     hz
#>   <int> <chr>          <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1  2025 KfS           720003 5644156 12757.
#> 2  2025 LK             30786  482985  6374.

In a full panel the same code gives the urban and rural series for all of Germany from 2013 onwards.

Use case 2: sex of the suspects

The share of female suspects by district and year:

tot$female_share <- round(tot$suspects_female / tot$suspects * 100, 1)
tot[tot$year %in% c(2019, 2025), c("year", "region_name_official", "suspects", "female_share")]
#> # A tibble: 10 × 4
#>     year region_name_official          suspects female_share
#>    <int> <chr>                            <dbl>        <dbl>
#>  1  2019 Flensburg, Stadt                 3450          23.5
#>  2  2019 Hamburg, Freie und Hansestadt   66216          22.5
#>  3  2019 Göttingen                        8774          24.8
#>  4  2019 Berlin, Stadt                  136704          26.4
#>  5  2019 Wartburgkreis                    3605.         23.5
#>  6  2025 Flensburg, Stadt                 3650          26.5
#>  7  2025 Hamburg, Freie und Hansestadt   64045          24  
#>  8  2025 Göttingen                        9703          25.4
#>  9  2025 Berlin, Stadt                  132281          25.9
#> 10  2025 Wartburgkreis                    3459          26.3

Use case 3: non-German suspects with and without immigration offences

The share of non-German suspects depends on whether offences against the Residence and Asylum Acts are counted. Comparing ------ (all offences) with 890000 (without them) shows how much:

y25 <- d[d$year == 2025, ]
y25$non_german_share <- round(y25$suspects_non_german / y25$suspects * 100, 1)
wide <- merge(
  y25[y25$offence_key == "------", c("region_name_official", "non_german_share")],
  y25[y25$offence_key == "890000", c("region_name_official", "non_german_share")],
  by = "region_name_official", suffixes = c("_all", "_without_725000")
)
wide
#>            region_name_official non_german_share_all
#> 1                 Berlin, Stadt                 47.3
#> 2              Flensburg, Stadt                 35.8
#> 3                     Göttingen                 33.4
#> 4 Hamburg, Freie und Hansestadt                 52.9
#> 5                 Wartburgkreis                 22.0
#>   non_german_share_without_725000
#> 1                            43.3
#> 2                            34.5
#> 3                            32.3
#> 4                            47.4
#> 5                            21.9

A share of suspects is not a crime rate of a population group: for that, the number of non-German suspects has to be divided by the non-German population, which the PKS does not publish, and the caveats of rule 3 apply.

Use case 4: firearm cases

Firearm cases are rare, so single district years are noisy. Pool several years before computing a rate per 100,000 inhabitants:

pooled <- dplyr::summarise(
  dplyr::group_by(tot, region_name_official),
  threatened = sum(firearm_threatened), fired = sum(firearm_fired),
  person_years = sum(pop), .groups = "drop"
)
pooled$fired_per_100k <- pooled$fired / pooled$person_years * 1e5
pooled
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   region_name_official          threatened  fired person_years fired_per_100k
#>   <chr>                              <dbl>  <dbl>        <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 Berlin, Stadt                     2564   2427      25758774            9.42
#> 2 Flensburg, Stadt                    80     50        646022            7.74
#> 3 Göttingen                          154    115       2286819            5.03
#> 4 Hamburg, Freie und Hansestadt      913    649      13001128            4.99
#> 5 Wartburgkreis                       30.0   61.9     1115339.           5.55

With the full data

The same columns come with every request to a data release from 2026.2 on, as published and harmonized:

# All districts, total offences, 2013 to 2025, harmonized to the latest boundary
panel <- pksR::pks_get(years = 2013:2025, offence = "total")

# As published: the districts and names of each year
published <- pksR::pks_get(years = 2013:2025, offence = "total", harmonize_to = NULL)

# Harmonized to another boundary year: the detail counts move with the
# crosswalk weights like the case counts
p2016 <- pksR::pks_get(years = 2013:2016, offence = "total", harmonize_to = 2016)

pks_validate() checks a panel; for the detail columns check in addition that suspects_male + suspects_female equals suspects and that suspects_non_german and the firearm counts do not exceed their totals. The pipeline stops a release when one of these fails.

Without R

The Parquet files of a release hold all columns. The per-year CSV files keep the columns of release 2026.1 and have a twin pks_kreis_<year>_<variant>_details.csv.gz with year, ags, offence_key and the detail columns, in the same row order; join them on these three columns. The official names come from boundary_map.csv of the release (columns to_name of the last period for the latest boundary).
